proceedings.outcome: the applicant was interviewed concerning his activities in Domachevo
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 1 and 3 April 1996, the applicant was interviewed by the British police concerning his activities in Domachevo during the German occupation.

proceedings.outcome: the applicant was interviewed concerning his activities in Domachevo
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 1 and 3 April 1996, the applicant was interviewed by the British police concerning his activities in Domachevo during the German occupation.

proceedings.outcome: application to stay trial as an abuse was refused
proceedings.supporting_quote: the defence made a number of applications: that the trial should be stayed as an abuse on the basis that due inter alia to the lapse of time since events the applicant could not obtain a fair trial. The application was refused by the trial judge

proceedings.outcome: evidence of two witnesses was ruled relevant and admissible
proceedings.supporting_quote: The defence also made an application that the evidence of two witnesses, Ivan Baglay and Evgeny Melianuk, be excluded as inadmissible. On 8 February 1999, the judge ruled that the evidence of both witnesses was relevant and admissible

proceedings.outcome: evidence of two witnesses was ruled to go before the jury
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 8 February 1999, the judge ruled that the evidence of both witnesses was relevant and admissible and, on 26 February 1999, that it should go before the jury.

proceedings.outcome: applicant was acquitted on counts 2 and 4
proceedings.supporting_quote: At the close of the prosecution case, the judge ruled that there was insufficient evidence as a matter of law to support a conviction on counts 2 and 4 and that the applicant should be acquitted.

proceedings.outcome: application to call evidence to prove provenance of document was refused
proceedings.supporting_quote: The prosecution made an application to the judge to call evidence to prove the provenance of the missing persons document in order to rebut the allegation of fabrication. On 24 March 1999, the judge refused the application.
On 25 March 1999, before the closing speeches were due to begin and a long adjournment over a weekend, the judge after consulting counsel decided to withdraw the applicant’s bail.

proceedings.outcome: application to review bail was refused
proceedings.supporting_quote: An application was made to the High Court to review bail on 26 March 1999. It was refused.
On 29 March 1999, defence counsel made representations... the trial judge reinstated bail.

proceedings.outcome: applicant was convicted of counts 1 and 3
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 1 April 1999, the jury convicted the applicant of counts 1 and 3.

proceedings.outcome: applicant was sentenced to life imprisonment
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 1 April 1999, the jury convicted the applicant of counts 1 and 3. The applicant was sentenced to a mandatory term of life imprisonment.
In its judgment of 10 February 2000, the Court of Appeal rejected the applicant’s appeal.

proceedings.outcome: petition for leave to appeal was refused
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 15 June 2000, the House of Lords refused the petition for leave to appeal.
